authorization.note: six spikes at 0.40 USD, S0-F fast map 0.40 plus full map 1.50

model: haiku (every run, plus CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku for subagents)

S0-A.question: Which Bash permission strategy lets /gsd-map-codebase --fast complete under dontAsk, and does the GSD preamble pass the permission layer?

cases.outcome: Narrow Bash allow list, hook logs only: all four fast-map files written, no denials. The model never ran the verbatim preamble; it improvised shorter commands.
Blanket Bash allow: all four files written; the model also tried git add and commit, which the sandbox refused (index.lock).
No Bash allow, allow-preamble hook: all four files written, no denials. The hook never fired an allow, so Bash ran for another reason (see A5).
Narrow list plus allow-preamble hook: all four files written, no denials.
Control, no skill and no Bash allow: the exact preamble plus gsd_run, node -e and a write outside the write set were all denied by the permission layer.
Control, hook deny-all, no skill: the Bash call was blocked by the hook before it ran.
Fast-map skill under a deny-all hook: Bash and Read were blocked, no map file written. A hook deny holds against the skill.

A5 prompt with the allow-preamble hook: the preamble plus gsd_run runtime-identity ran (identity JSON in the tool result), node -e and the outside write were denied. A hook allow is honored under dontAsk for a command no rule allows.

findings: All four fast-map files exist for every strategy A1 to A4. The skill frontmatter (allowed-tools includes Bash) pre-approves Bash while the skill runs, so permissions.allow text rules never constrain a skill-driven run; A5 shows the same commands denied without the skill.

In the full map (F2) the post-notification steps (stamp-codebase-map plus a secret scan, a compound command) were denied under dontAsk in the main session: the skill grant does not cover later turns. AVARICE runs stamp-codebase-map itself.
Hook allow (A8) and hook deny (A6, A7) both work in -p under dontAsk. A hook deny overrides the skill grant.
The model does not reliably copy the preamble verbatim, so a first-line byte match is a narrow allow, not a requirement for success.
The fast map needs Read of ~/.claude/gsd-core (the skill tells the model to read workflows/scan.md); the cases grant Read(//<gsd-core>/**).
The host creates an empty .claude/.cc-writes directory in the working directory; the staging diff gate must tolerate it (git ignores empty directories).
Default commit_docs is true in a scratch repository and the model attempted a commit (A2); staging config must set commit_docs false, and .git stays denyWrite.

preamble.firstLine: _GSD_SHIM_NAME="gsd-tools.cjs"; _GSD_RUNTIME_ROOT="${RUNTIME_DIR:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)}"; GSD_TOOLS="${_GSD_RUNTIME_ROOT}/gsd-core/bin/${_GSD_SHIM_NAME}"; _gsd_at() { for _p; do if [ -f "$_p" ]; then GSD_TOOLS="$_p"; return 0; fi; done; return 1; }; _gsd_id_ok() { case "$("$1" runtime-identity --raw 2>/dev/null || true)" in '{"packageName":"@opengsd/gsd-core"'*'}') return 0;; *) return 1;; esac; }; _gsd_homes() { set -- "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}" "${ANTIGRAVITY_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.gemini/antigravity}" "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity-ide" "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity-cli" "${AUGMENT_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.augment}" "${CLINE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.cline}" "${CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.codebuddy}" "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}" "${COPILOT_CONFIG_DIR:-${COPILOT_HOME:-$HOME/.copilot}}" "${CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.cursor}" "${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}" "${KILO_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/kilo}" "${KIMI_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.config/agents}" "$HOME/.agents" "${KIMI_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.kimi-code}" "${OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode}" "${PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR:-$HOME/.pi/agent}" "${QWEN_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.qwen}" "${TRAE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.trae}" "${WINDSURF_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.codeium/windsurf}" "${ZCODE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.zcode}" "${GROK_AGENTS_HOME:-$HOME/.agents}"; for _h; do _gsd_at "$_h/gsd-core/bin/${_GSD_SHIM_NAME}" && return 0; done; return 1; }; if _gsd_at "${_GSD_RUNTIME_ROOT}/gsd-core/bin/${_GSD_SHIM_NAME}" "${_GSD_RUNTIME_ROOT}/.claude/gsd-core/bin/${_GSD_SHIM_NAME}" "${_GSD_RUNTIME_ROOT}/.codex/gsd-core/bin/${_GSD_SHIM_NAME}"; then gsd_run() { node "$GSD_TOOLS" "$@"; }; elif _gsd_homes; then gsd_run() { node "$GSD_TOOLS" "$@"; }; elif unset -f gsd_run; _G="$(command -v gsd_run)"; [ -n "$_G" ] && _gsd_id_ok "$_G"; then GSD_TOOLS="$_G"; gsd_run() { "$GSD_TOOLS" "$@"; }; else echo "ERROR: gsd-tools.cjs not found at $GSD_TOOLS and no identity-proving gsd_run is on PATH. Run: npx -y @opengsd/gsd-core@latest --claude --local" >&2; exit 1; fi; GSD_IDENTITY_STATUS=unverified; _gsd_id_ok gsd_run && GSD_IDENTITY_STATUS=ok; export GSD_IDENTITY_STATUS; [ "$GSD_IDENTITY_STATUS" = ok ] || echo "WARNING: \"$GSD_TOOLS\" did not prove it is @opengsd/gsd-core - it is either a different package or an @opengsd/gsd-core older than the runtime-identity verb. See docs/how-to/diagnose-a-foreign-gsd-tools.md" >&2; if [ -n "${CLAUDE_ENV_FILE:-}" ] && [ -n "${GSD_TOOLS:-}" ]; then printf "export PATH='%s':\"\$PATH\"\n" "${GSD_TOOLS%/*}" >> "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; fi

S0-A.recommendation: Do not use permissions.allow Bash text rules as the command-identity control: skills pre-approve Bash and the preamble is a 2.5 KB compound line. Use the sandbox for effects and the AVARICE PreToolUse hook for identity: deny by default, allow the preamble line (match by SHA-256 of the first line, fingerprinted at inspect) followed only by gsd_run read verbs, plus a small read-only set. Keep Read(//<gsd-core>/**) allowed, set commit_docs false, and run stamp-codebase-map from AVARICE after the map.

S0-B.question: Can a contained invocation move a ref or write git config in the source repository, per staging strategy?

cases.outcome: Linked worktree, no extra denyWrite: refs/heads/main of the SOURCE repository was moved (update-ref and branch -f succeeded), git commit succeeded (one object, worktree HEAD moved). Config writes failed (echo redirect denied by the permission layer, git config could not lock the file).
Linked worktree, denyWrite on the source .git and the worktree gitdir: every git write failed (update-ref, branch -f, commit, config); source refs, HEAD and config byte-identical.
Local clone with denyWrite on the clone .git: clone and source refs, HEAD and config unchanged; writes to the source .git by absolute path (update-ref, config, redirect) also failed.

denyRead on the source checkout root with allowRead of its .git: cat of .env denied by the permission rule, node readFileSync failed with EPERM (OS layer), git log in the worktree worked; the fake secret never appeared in any tool result.

S0-B.recommendation: A linked worktree is safe only with generated denyWrite entries on the source .git and the worktree gitdir (B2); without them a mapper moves a source branch ref (B1). Onboarding needs no commits (commit_docs false, diff gate), so B2 costs nothing. Prefer the local clone for staging (B3): it holds no shared ref store with the user repository, so safety does not depend on a generated denyWrite being present. If the worktree is kept, preflight must assert the two denyWrite entries and a post-run digest of for-each-ref, HEAD and config. Use denyRead on the source checkout root with allowRead of its .git (B4) in either case.

S0-C.question: Does gsd_run resolve inside the contained Bash tool with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-edu?

cases.outcome: PATH with ~/.claude/gsd-core/bin first: the verbatim preamble then gsd_run runtime-identity --raw returned {"packageName":"@opengsd/gsd-core","version":"1.17.0"} in the tool result.
Control without the PATH entry: "ERROR: gsd-tools.cjs not found ... no identity-proving gsd_run is on PATH" in the tool result.

findings: Under env -i the host reports "Not logged in" unless USER is in the environment (macOS credential lookup); with USER set the login under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-edu works. LOGNAME is harmless.
The contained Bash tool runs zsh: the preamble prints the harmless "(eval):unset:1: no such hash table element: gsd_run" line before succeeding.
S0-C.recommendation: Give every invocation PATH=<gsd-core>/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin (verified fix (a) of research Pitfall 1); add USER and LOGNAME to the env allowlist next to HOME, LANG, TMPDIR and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Preflight runs the preamble plus runtime-identity with the generated environment and maps failure to blocked/adapter_incompatible.

S0-D.question: Which form drives gsd-intel-updater under -p: --agent, or the Agent tool with a background subagent?

cases.outcome: claude -p --agent gsd-intel-updater "focus: full; project root: ." with the agent supplied only through --agents: resolved; five intel files plus .last-refresh.json written under .planning/intel, gsd_run intel validate reported valid. The session had no Agent tool (zero subagents).

Agent tool with subagent_type gsd-intel-updater and run_in_background true: also wrote five valid files; the -p process stayed alive about 31 s although the main turn lasted 2.5 s, and the files existed when it exited, so -p waited for the background agent.

findings: Glob was not available in either session (the agent fell back to find through Bash).
/gsd-map-codebase --query ... has no intel workflow behind it (E3 and research); only the agent form works.
S0-D.recommendation: Use the D1 form: claude -p --agent gsd-intel-updater "focus: full; project root: <staging>" with the agent in the generated --agents file. It needs no Agent tool, so the intel subagent budget is 0. AVARICE runs config-set intel.enabled true before launch; write set .planning/intel, with .planning/config.json in denyWrite. Cost and time were about 0.009 USD and 31 s for a 5-file repository.

S0-E.question: With --setting-sources "", do CLAUDE.md files, auto memory and skills load?

cases.outcome: Disable variables set, "say hello": no canary, no auto-memory path in the init event.
Disable variables set, direct probe: canary NONE, graphify instruction no.
No disable variables, "say hello": no canary in the reply, but the init event lists memory_paths.auto under ~/.claude-edu/projects.
No disable variables, direct probe: canary NONE, graphify instruction no (neither the repository CLAUDE.md nor the global CLAUDE.md loaded); memory_paths.auto present.
Positive control, --setting-sources project: the probe quotes the canary and reports the graphify instruction, so the probe can detect a load.

--plugin-dir with skills symlinked: the init event lists avarice-run-skills:gsd-map-codebase and avarice-run-skills:graphify; /gsd-map-codebase --query status expanded the skill body (the model reasoned from its text), and the --agents entries appear under bare names.

S0-E.recommendation: --setting-sources "" alone keeps both the repository CLAUDE.md and the user CLAUDE.md out of the invocation (E2b against the E4 control). Auto memory is still switched on in that mode (memory_paths.auto in E2 and E2b), so set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 (E1, E1b show no memory path); CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1 is harmless belt and braces. Skills load only through the generated --plugin-dir and appear namespaced; agents through --agents under bare names.

S0-F.question: What do a fast map and a full four-agent map cost in dollars, time and tool calls on a scratch clone of ~/aa-phan-portfolio-v2?

cases.outcome: Fast map, first attempt: the mapper subagent was auto-backgrounded, produced 9 tool calls in 70 s, then stalled; the host stopped it at its 10-minute background wait ceiling. No map file written. A transient stall, recorded as a finding.
Fast map, retry: four files (STACK 109, INTEGRATIONS 93, ARCHITECTURE 269, STRUCTURE 248 lines), one mapper subagent.
Full map: seven documents, four background mappers; the closing stamp-codebase-map and secret scan were denied (see S0-A). 82 hook-logged tool calls.

S0-F.recommendation: Measured on haiku against the 363-file target: fast map 0.04 USD in 147 s, full map 0.13 USD in 171 s with 4 subagents and 82 tool calls. Default onboarding budgets: wallClockMinutes map 8, intel 5, knowledge 6; invocations 4; toolCalls 300; subagentsTotal 4 (map) + 0 (intel, --agent form) + 1 per 20 documents (knowledge); costUsd.perInvocation 1.00 and perRun 3.00 (about 8x and 7x the measured sums, and only valid for the haiku mapper model); retry 1. AVARICE must enforce its own wall clock with SIGTERM: a stalled background subagent holds -p open for the host ceiling of 10 minutes (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS), and a stalled run still reports almost no cost.

S0-G.question: Does the /graphify knowledge pass run under the real sandbox with no network and only the corpus directory writable?

cases.outcome: graphify directory not on PATH: interpreter resolution failed (uv could not write its cache; python3 has no graphify), the install fallbacks tried the network and were refused at the proxy; no graph.

graphify on PATH: interpreter resolved from the graphify shebang, detect found 4 documents; the run stopped when the model could not Read the skill reference file (plugin path outside the Read allow list).

graphify on PATH plus Read of the plugin skill path and ~/.claude/skills/graphify: full run; graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.html, manifest.json, cost.json and cache/ written under graphify-out/ in the cwd; the one document-chunk subagent used the general-purpose type.

measured.uvNetworkAttempted: yes in G1 (install fallback, refused at the proxy); no in G3 (uv failed earlier on its cache directory write)
measured.maxWorkersNote: a document-only pass runs no AST extraction (code files 0), so no multiprocessing; --max-workers 1 stays required for any code extraction under the sandbox

findings: The knowledge-pass subagent tags document edges EXTRACTED (16 of 21), which S-45 forbids; AVARICE must re-tag or reject them after the pass.
No node carries _origin; AVARICE stamps model-origin nodes itself so the deterministic and model parts stay distinguishable.
graph.json has no built_at_commit; the AVARICE merge stamps it.
Step 1 of the skill is unreliable under the sandbox (uv cannot write ~/.cache/uv); resolution works only through the graphify shebang interpreter.
S0-G.recommendation: For the knowledge invocation put the directory of the graphify binary on PATH (only for that invocation) so the shebang interpreter resolves, grant Read on the generated plugin skill path and on ~/.claude/skills/graphify, keep the corpus directory as cwd and the only writable path, and deny the network. Output lands in <corpus>/graphify-out; expect one subagent per document chunk. No --max-workers flag is needed for documents. Post-process the graph: re-tag document edges to INFERRED or AMBIGUOUS, stamp _origin and built_at_commit, drop dangling edges.

notes: Transcripts stay under $SPIKE_ROOT (outside every repository and Claude config directory); evidence/*.json holds digests only.
The spend ledger counts every run including reruns and the env-bisect runs recorded as P0-debug (0.02 USD, a conservative upper bound).
Target repository ~/aa-phan-portfolio-v2: git status --porcelain (only "?? .env"), for-each-ref digest and HEAD unchanged after all runs.
